summary: You take 30 units of graduate Sociology courses (numbered 200 and above) for a letter grade, not counting workshops or the colloquium, with at most 5 units of independent study or directed research (SOC 390, SOC 391) and 5 units of a statistics or methods course from another department, which you move in by hand. Your 3.0 GPA, and that you enrolled under the SOC listing rather than a cross-listing, are checked by hand.

limits.label: statistics or methods course in another department

add.why: "A minimum of 30 graduate-level units. All 30 units for the minor must be in courses taught by faculty appointed in the Department of Sociology. Students must enroll in the SOC course offerings (not cross-listed sections). Workshops and colloquia do not count towards the PhD minor. Exceptions: Five (5) of these units may be taken as an independent study or directed reading with a member of Department of Sociology faculty. Another five (5) units may be taken in a statistics or methods course taught in another department." Graduate level is read as numbered 200 and above. "Workshops and colloquia do not count towards the PhD minor." (the SOC workshops and SOC 396 are excluded) "Five (5) of these units may be taken as an independent study or directed reading" (SOC 390 Graduate Individual Study and SOC 391 Graduate Directed Research, 5 units between them).
GPA: "A grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) or better."

program.why: Grading: "All units must be taken for a letter grade."
